# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your delivery reality, not your wishes**
Map what your coaches *actually deliver right now* — not what you plan to offer in six months. Audit 3-4 typical member journeys this week. Document: class types, one-on-one formats, nutrition check-ins, progress tracking, whatever's real. This becomes your honest baseline menu.

**2. Price by value extraction, not cost-plus guessing**
Don't calculate "hourly rate × hours." Instead: interview 5-8 members who've paid for premium add-ons (extra PT sessions, nutrition plans, challenges). What problem did they solve? What would they *have paid* for it? Price the *outcome*, not the time. This justifies premium tiers your coaches can actually sell.

**3. Create TWO separate menus with different language**
**Coach menu** = operational (what they deliver, duration, prerequisites, upsell triggers). **Member menu** = benefit-driven (what you'll achieve, who it's for, what's included vs. add-ons). Members don't care about your process; they care about their result. The coach version drives accountability; the member version drives conversion.

**4. Test and lock it in writing within 7 days**
Get draft versions into your coaches' hands. Ask: "Can you sell this? Is anything missing?" Revise once. Publish as a simple one-pager (PDF, printed laminate for the gym floor). Ambiguity kills sales — specificity moves inventory.

**5. Build your first upsell path into the menu itself**
Show the base offer, then explicitly show what *one step up* looks like

## REVENUE — BIGGEST PRIORITY: FIX CHURN & REV/MEMBER COLLAPSE

**The problem:** Sept is your best absolute month (£22,016, 168 members) but revenue *per member* has crashed to £131 — down from £145 in July and £139 in April. You're adding members but each one generates less cash. That's a pricing or mix problem, not a volume win.

• **Audit your membership tiers right now.** You're likely signing too many new members on intro/discount rates or lower-tier plans. Sept added 15 net members (153→168) but rev/member fell 10%. Either lock new joiners onto full price after 3 months, or shift the new-member offer from price cuts to 1-to-1 PT sessions (upsell, not discount).

• **Attack the May churn spike (12.8%) — it's your outlier.** Post-Easter lull? Summer holidays starting? Identify the cohort that churned and test a targeted retention play (e.g. free July class pass, partner discount, accountability challenge). Keeping just 2–3 of those lost members would add £250+/month ongoing.

• **Upsell class packs + PT to your growing base.** You've got 168 active members; unlimited membership alone isn't scaling revenue fast enough. Launch a tiered upsell: beginner PT block (4 sessions, £80), advanced class pass add-on (8 sessions, £60). Target 20% attachment in Q4 — that's +£1,500/month with near-zero marginal cost.
